_comment: The AI voiceover. Each cue starts at `at` seconds, lined up with the scene it describes. {key} is replaced by that number from artifacts/report/numbers.json. Edit the words freely; run `npm run voice` to regenerate. A line that runs into the next cue is spoken slightly faster (up to max_speed); if it still does not fit, the script stops and names it.

cues.text: Stock Tokens trade all weekend. Their price feeds don't.
Over {oracle.weekends} weekends, {oracle.feeds_without_update} of {oracle.feeds} feeds posted nothing, Friday night to Sunday night.
No prices, no liquidations. When Monday opens with a gap, lenders take the loss.
Afterhours is a Morpho vault for Stock Tokens.
Each stock gets three markets. It lends in the riskiest one its own last year allows.
Before every close, it forecasts each stock's bad night. Too risky? It pulls the money borrowers aren't using.
And every move gets a reason card, with its fingerprint written onchain for anyone to check.
Fixed mixes sit on this line. Afterhours sits above it: same yield, {rel.b_vs_blend.bad_debt_less} less bad debt, {rel.b_vs_blend.worst_less} smaller worst night.
Against a yearly plan: {rel.b_vs_fixed_map.bad_debt_less} less bad debt, {rel.b_vs_fixed_map.worst_less} smaller worst night.
We wrote the test down before running it. Our first design didn't pass, so the simpler one ships.
Honest note: the rates are modelled. Real markets pay lenders {market.supply_apy} today.
The next morning, it opens {replay.gap} down.
At the top limit, a vault lost {replay.always_weekday.bad_debt} USDG. Afterhours had already pulled back, and lost {replay.afterhours.bad_debt}: {rel.replay.b_less} less.
The market is early. When we measured, {market.stock_token_markets} Morpho markets took Stock Tokens as collateral: {market.usdg_supplied} USDG supplied, {market.usdg_borrowed} borrowed.
We're building the vault lenders can trust with it, as it grows.
Built on Robinhood Chain and Morpho. Try it live, and read every line of the code on GitHub.
